question: What did Stellar's June 2026 Quantum Preparedness Plan commit to, and which quantum-safe features were still roadmap items?

golden.answer: SDF published the Quantum Preparedness Plan on June 9, 2026 as a three-stage roadmap, not a claim that Stellar is already quantum-safe. Stage 1 adds ML-DSA-44 and ML-DSA-65 signature-verification host functions for Soroban contract accounts during 2026. Every account is expected to be able to add a quantum-safe signer by the end of 2027 through a native protocol upgrade. Those primitives did not exist at publication.
keyFacts: SDF published the Quantum Preparedness Plan on June 9, 2026.
The plan is a three-stage roadmap, not a shipped capability.
Stage 1 plans ML-DSA-44/65 verification host functions for contract accounts in 2026.
Every account is expected able to add a quantum-safe signer by end of 2027.
avoid: Do NOT claim ML-DSA host functions or a native quantum-safe signer had shipped when the plan was published.
Do NOT present the 2026/2027 targets as guaranteed dates.
golden.notes: Grade what the plan said at publication. Accept later sourced developments, including Bell (Protocol 30, CAP-0087) and a sourced Mainnet activation.

truth.notes: Grade what the June 2026 plan said at publication. Later developments are optional. As of 2026-11-10, Bell/P30 is live on Testnet with CAP-0087 ML-DSA-44/65/87 contract verification. Pubnet still runs P29 and the Bell Mainnet vote is scheduled for 2026-11-23. SDF still describes a native post-quantum signer for classic accounts as a future change. The June roadmap also leaves deprecation timing dependent on the threat. Accept a later sourced Mainnet activation.
